hero.lead: A nation of 83.5 million whose Finance Agency plans about €512 billion of federal securities in 2026, as a €500 billion special fund for infrastructure and climate neutrality begins to invest.

capital.heading: A €500 billion fund to rebuild, and every child a reader.

record.text: Federal securities planned for 2026: about €318 billion in capital market auctions, €176 billion in money market paper and €16 to €19 billion in green securities
Special fund for infrastructure and climate neutrality: €300 billion for federal investment, €100 billion for the Länder and municipalities, €100 billion for the Climate and Transformation Fund
Startchancen programme, 2024 to 2034: up to €1 billion a year from the federal government, matched by the Länder, for about 4,000 schools with many socially disadvantaged pupils
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: Federal securities, 2026
register.detail: German Finance Agency · issuance plan of 18 December 2025 · about €318bn in capital market securities, €176bn in money market paper, €16bn to €19bn in green securities · fourth-quarter plan of 24 September 2026 unchanged
register.note: The Finance Agency states that €17 billion of green federal securities were placed in 2026
register.text: The Federal Republic plans to raise about €512 billion in 2026 through federal bonds and notes, Treasury discount paper (Bubills) and green federal securities, and to issue a 20-year federal bond for the first time. The plan for the fourth quarter, published on 24 September 2026, left the annual outlook of December 2025 unchanged. It is the sovereign’s own market funding, and its green securities finance federal spending on transport, energy and resources, research, international cooperation and ecosystems.

register.name: Special fund for infrastructure and climate neutrality
register.detail: Federal Ministry of Finance · Monthly Report, March 2026
register.note: €300 billion for federal investment, €100 billion for the Länder and municipalities and €100 billion for the Climate and Transformation Fund
register.text: Investment by the federal government, the Länder and municipalities, and the Climate and Transformation Fund.

register.name: Federal financial assistance for social housing, programme year 2026
register.detail: Federal Ministry for Housing, Urban Development and Building · administrative agreements for 2026 and 2027 in force, 20 March 2026 · of which €500M for Junges Wohnen
register.note: The Bund plans €5 billion for programme year 2027 and €23.5 billion in all up to 2029
register.text: Federal grants to the Länder for social housing in programme year 2026, including €500 million for Junges Wohnen, housing for students and trainees. The Länder funded about 62,000 social housing units in 2024, and the ministry states its aim of reversing the decline in the social housing stock. It serves the shelter standard.
by: Federal Ministry for Housing, Urban Development and Building

register.name: Green federal bond 2026 (2041), the first 15-year green Bund
register.detail: German Finance Agency · priced 3 March 2026 by syndicate, settled 10 March 2026 · due 15 May 2041 · coupon 2.6% · reoffer yield 3.140% · greenium of 1 basis point · order book above €22bn
register.note: Volume of €4 billion including €1 billion retained; ISIN DE000BU3F007
register.text: The inaugural 15-year green federal bond, placed after the federal government published the second version of its green bond framework on 15 January 2026. Green federal securities finance federal expenditure on transport, international cooperation, research, energy and resources, and ecosystems; the energy expenditure serves the energy standard.

register.name: KfW promotional business in Germany, 2025
register.detail: KfW · report for the financial year 2025 · loans and grants · housing, including building promotion, €24.2bn · SMEs and founders €23.5bn · Renewable Energies Standard programme €9.2bn
register.note: The core domestic promotional business, up from €45.8 billion in 2024
register.text: The domestic loans and grants of KfW, Germany’s state-owned promotional bank, in 2025. Its commitments of €24.2 billion for housing, including the federal funding for efficient buildings, serve the shelter and energy standards, and €9.2 billion under its Renewable Energies Standard programme serves the energy standard.

register.name: Startchancen programme for schools in challenging circumstances
register.detail: Federal Ministry of Education, Family Affairs, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth and the Länder · 2024 to 2034 · up to €1bn a year from the Bund, matched by the Länder · about 4,000 schools in 2026
register.note: Started on 1 August 2024 with 2,125 schools; about 60% of the pupils it supports are in primary school
register.text: A ten-year federal and Länder programme for about 4,000 schools with a high share of socially disadvantaged pupils, about one million in all: investment in the learning environment, opportunity budgets for each school and staff for multi-professional teams. Its aim is to halve the number of pupils at these schools who miss the minimum standards in mathematics and German, which serves the education standard, the standard furthest from reach in Germany.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: Council of the EU · Approved 16 July 2024 · EU Recovery and Resilience Facility
register.text: EU funding, in grants, for agreed reforms and investments.

register.name: Hamburg electricity distribution grid (Hamburg Energienetze)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · framework loan signed 19 May 2026 · first funds available from October 2025 · 28% of a programme of about €2.9bn to 2029 · about 1,500 km of new and renewed lines
register.note: Hamburg Energienetze is a holding of HGV, the group holding company of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg
register.text: A framework loan to modernise and expand Hamburg’s electricity distribution grid, where the EIB expects peak load at least to double with heat pumps, electric mobility and zero-emission buses. It serves the energy standard; on the same day the EIB signed a further €125 million with vhh.mobility for 188 electric buses.

register.name: Social and affordable rental housing in Berlin (Gewobag)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 5 May 2026 · up to €300M · around 1,465 social and affordable rental homes, including student accommodation
register.note: Gewobag is wholly owned by the State of Berlin and manages more than 70,000 homes
register.text: An EIB loan to co-finance the construction of around 1,465 social and affordable rental homes in Berlin, including student accommodation. It serves the shelter standard; the EIB states that its housing investment in Germany totalled €674 million in 2025.

register.name: Electricity grid in West Mecklenburg (WEMAG)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · signed 12 November 2025, announced 9 January 2026 · more than one third of the grid investments planned for the next four years
register.note: WEMAG has been majority-owned by the municipalities it supplies since January 2010; WEMAG Netz plans €1.2 billion of grid investment by 2033
register.text: An investment financing agreement to expand the power grid of West Mecklenburg, in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, so that it can take more solar power, rooftop photovoltaics, heat pumps and charging stations. It serves the energy standard with a reliable supply of renewable electricity.

register.name: Energy investment risk-sharing with Commerzbank (Growth for Energy)
register.detail: European Investment Bank · agreed 21 November 2025 · EIB covers up to 50% of Commerzbank’s risk on eligible energy loans · renewable generation, grid reinforcement and district heating, mainly for municipal utilities
register.note: The financing programme for new energy investment; the EIB share is cover for up to half of the risk
register.text: A risk-sharing arrangement under the EIB’s Growth for Energy initiative that lets Commerzbank lend more for renewable electricity generation, grid reinforcement and modern district heating, mainly to Stadtwerke, the municipal utilities. It serves the energy standard.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 13.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
